summary: The core loop has good bones: the WebApp ends every job with a message after its window, idempotent sends, an email outbox that never double-sends, and a two-hour watch that notices when an upload never reaches the Pipeline. But the one Pipeline host keeps every job state and money record with no backup, and the backup alarm is built to stay quiet when backup was never set up. Several real failures end work for good or wait for an operator command: a provider key or billing error fails every in-flight room build at once, a 36-hour email outage cancels introductions the site can never ask for again, outcome questions stop silently when a site closes its job, and large picked videos are cut by the server's 5-minute request limit. Two of the known red browser tests are wrong tests, not product bugs, and the core journey test checks emails only as queued, which is how the Reply-To bug got through.

findings.title: The one control-plane host has no backup of job state and money records, and the alarm stays quiet
evidence: cmd: operator_door.py journal blueprint-control-plane-state-backup.service -n 15 -> every run 11:55Z to 15:32Z 2026-11-22: 'was skipped because of an unmet condition check (ConditionPathExists=/etc/blueprint/control-plane-backup/b2_bucket)'
door-status.json capacity.stall.checks.state_backup = {"status": "not_configured"}
pipeline:src/blueprint_pipeline/control_plane_state_backup.py:556-562 ('not_configured (no ledger, so never set up: quiet)')
door-status.json capacity.alerts: no control_plane_backup_stale among 18 alerts
pipeline:docs/runbooks/beta-operations.md:56 (control_plane_backup_stale is documented as paging after 2 h)
findings.today: Every job's state, every money ledger and receipt lives on one DigitalOcean droplet. The backup unit has run every 15 minutes since it shipped and skipped every time because its bucket file was never installed. The alarm treats 'never set up' as quiet, so nobody is told. If the disk or droplet is lost, every in-flight job and the month's money records go with it.
findings.should: Either a backup runs, or the owner sees one standing alert that it does not.
findings.proposal: Two lines of work, one PR plus one owner step: (1) in control_plane_state_backup's stall reading, report not_configured as a warning alert on the capacity summary, not quiet; (2) owner installs /etc/blueprint/control-plane-backup/b2_bucket and its key (or names another bucket). Do not add a new gate.
findings.user_result: The owner learns today that a host loss would erase job state and money records, and can close it in an hour.
findings.risk: The alert adds one standing warning until the bucket is set. Backups cost B2 storage (small; the state is not media).
findings.requirement_source: AGENTS.md spend limits and money records (money hard stop); runbook 'Control-plane state backup and host rebuild'

findings.title: A provider key or billing refusal fails every in-flight room build for good; only a per-job operator command reopens them
findings.journey_step: C.3 Reconstruction (World Labs) and C.2 preparation (Gemini, SAM, OpenAI)
evidence: pipeline:src/blueprint_pipeline/job_retry_policy.py:176 RETRY_LATER_STATUSES = {408, 409, 425, 429}
pipeline:src/blueprint_pipeline/job_retry_policy.py:192-200 request_cannot_succeed: any other 4xx (so 401, 402, 403)
pipeline:src/blueprint_pipeline/website_atlas_preview.py:315-320 a 'cannot succeed' code -> state failed now; 'an operator's retry reopens the job after a fix'
pipeline:docs/runbooks/beta-operations.md:64-73 failed Atlas jobs never page; 'Nothing steps a parked job again'; reopen only with door selected-handoff --atlas-retry
webapp:server/utils/websiteAtlasPreview.ts:122-127 the only site sentence for failed: 'A 3D preview could not be made from this recording.'
findings.today: An expired or rotated API key (401), an unpaid provider account (402) or a revoked permission (403) is treated as 'this request can never succeed'. Every job that hits it in that window ends failed at once. No alarm pages for failed jobs. After the key is fixed, an operator must reopen each job by hand with a door command. The site is never told why; its job ends when the 7-day window sweep runs.
findings.should: A refusal about Blueprint's own credentials or account is an outage: it pages once and the jobs wait and resume by themselves once the key works.
findings.proposal: In job_retry_policy, move 401 and 402 (and 403 when the provider body names the key or account) to the outage class that _outage_retry already handles until the job's deadline, and page once per provider on the first such refusal. One small PR plus tests.
findings.user_result: After a key rotation, jobs finish on their own instead of ending; no per-job operator command.
findings.risk: A genuine 403 for a forbidden request would be retried until the job window ends; the retries cost nothing because the provider refuses before work. Paid admission still applies to each retry.
findings.requirement_source: job_retry_policy (AGENTS.md: one retry rule); the per-job reopen requirement has source nobody, and doctrine forbids an operator command as the only way forward

findings.title: An email outage over 36 hours cancels introductions for good, and the site cannot ask again
evidence: webapp:server/utils/captureOutboxRetry.ts:29 MAX_UNDELIVERED_AGE_MS = 36 h
webapp:server/utils/captureOutbox.ts:201-206 a row refused past that age becomes failed
webapp:server/utils/jobIntroductionGate.ts:169-174 a failed company email cancels the introduction, clears both sides' details and voids the billable event
webapp:server/utils/jobIntroductions.ts:118-121 'One cancelled at dispatch is not made again: its emails' keys are spent' -> already_introduced
webapp:server/utils/jobCompanies.ts:530 canIntroduce is false for a cancelled pair; client/src/lib/siteIntroductions.ts:21 'This introduction could not go ahead. We did not give them your details.'
findings.today: If Resend refuses for 36 hours (quota, outage, revoked key) or the web process that sends email is down that long, every introduction queued then is cancelled. The site reads 'This introduction could not go ahead' and the Introduce us button never comes back for that company. Nobody can redo it short of editing records.
findings.should: A cancelled introduction caused by Blueprint's own email failure can be asked for again with the same one press.
findings.proposal: Key the introduction emails and billable event by attempt (for example append the cancelled count), and let canIntroduce be true again when cancelReason is company_email_failed or company_email_not_sent. One PR in jobIntroductions.ts and jobCompanies.ts with tests. Keep the void on the old billable event.
findings.user_result: The site presses Introduce us again after an outage instead of losing that company.
findings.risk: Two billable events for one pair (one void, one recorded); the invoice must count only recorded ones, which status already says.
findings.requirement_source: nobody for 'never again'; the void-on-failure rule comes from the introduction gate design (G3/H2) and protects money

findings.title: The 14, 45 and 90-day questions stop silently once a site closes its job
evidence: webapp:server/utils/jobOutcomeGate.ts:71-76 jobTakesOutcomeQuestions requires loadCompanyJobAccess(...).access.listed
webapp:server/utils/teamJobAccess.ts:237-241 closed_by_site and authority_ended make listed false

webapp:server/tests/job-outcomes.test.ts:137-142 'sends nothing ... while the job is not visible' pins it
findings.today: Outcome questions are asked only while the job is still listed for companies. A site that found its company and closes the job, or a job whose Pipeline authority ended, gets no question at 14, 45 or 90 days, and neither does the company. Nothing records that the question was skipped.
findings.should: Once an introduction exists, both sides are asked at 14, 45 and 90 days unless the site withdrew or someone gave a final answer.
findings.proposal: Replace the listing check in jobTakesOutcomeQuestions with only the withdrawal check (consent_revoked or capture_withdrawal). Update the one test. The outbox gate outcomeQuestionIsCurrent follows it.
findings.user_result: The owner learns what happened after every introduction, which is what a future invoice and investors need.
findings.risk: A site that closed its job gets up to three short emails; each email has five answers, and a final answer ends the questions.

findings.title: A picked video is sent in one request that the server cuts after 5 minutes, with no resume
evidence: webapp:client/src/lib/selfCaptureVideo.ts:115-160 the whole file in one XMLHttpRequest POST, client timeout 15 min, no parts or resume
webapp:server/index.ts:5 http.createServer with no requestTimeout set (grep requestTimeout in server/: no match); .nvmrc = 22
cmd: node slowpost.mjs (scratch; default http.createServer on node v22.23.5, a 400 MB POST at about 640 KB/s) -> 'requestTimeout 300000', 'response 408 after s 330.011' with about 210 MB sent
webapp:server/routes/self-capture-uploads.ts:128,146-147 the route accepts up to 2 GiB
findings.today: When a site picks a saved video instead of filming in the page, the browser sends the whole file in one request. Node 22 closes any request not fully received within 300 seconds, and the server does not change that. At a 10 Mbit/s phone uplink that is about 375 MB; at 5 Mbit/s about 190 MB. A longer upload fails and starts from zero on retry. A network drop or a closed tab also loses the whole upload.
findings.should: A picked video uploads in parts like the in-page recording does, and a retry resumes from the last stored part.
findings.proposal: Smallest fix today: set server.requestTimeout = 0 (or 30 min) for the upload route in server/index.ts so long uploads are not cut. Then send picked files through the existing parts route (/:token/parts/:index and /parts/complete, already used by CaptureRecorder) and use the existing GET /:token/parts to skip stored parts.
findings.user_result: A site on an ordinary phone connection can post a 1-2 minute video it already filmed.
findings.risk: Longer-held connections on the single web instance; the parts route already exists and is tested by the recorder.
findings.verify_how: Measured on a bare Node 22 server with the same defaults as server/index.ts (408 at 330 s). Not measured end to end through Render's proxy; a real phone upload of a 500 MB file to a staging deploy would settle it.
findings.requirement_source: doctrine 'video in'; the single-request design has source nobody

findings.title: An in-page recording cut by a closed tab or locked phone cannot be resumed
findings.journey_step: A.5 Film the job in the browser
evidence: webapp:client/src/components/site/CaptureRecorder.tsx:126-230 unsent parts live only in queueRef (page memory)
webapp:client/src/components/site/CaptureRecorder.tsx:60,217-224 after 4 attempts the page asks the site to press resume (works only while the page stays open)
grep visibilitychange|onended in CaptureRecorder.tsx -> no match (no handling of a track that ends when the phone locks or the tab is backgrounded)
webapp:server/routes/self-capture-uploads.ts:1010 GET /:token/parts exists; grep in client/src -> no caller
findings.today: Parts already sent are kept on the server, but parts still waiting are only in the page. Closing the tab, or the browser discarding a backgrounded tab, loses them. Locking the phone ends the camera track and nothing in the recorder reacts to that. After a reload there is no way to continue: the stored parts are never used and the site must film again.
findings.should: A cut recording either finishes with what was stored or the page says plainly 'film again' at once.
findings.proposal: On reload, call the existing GET /:token/parts and offer 'Send what was saved' (compose stored parts) or 'Film again'. Listen for the video track's ended event and stop the recording cleanly with the parts already queued.
findings.user_result: A site that locks its phone mid-recording keeps what it filmed.
findings.risk: A composed video with only the first parts may be too short; the first look will say so.
findings.verify_how: Code reading only; a real iOS Safari and Android Chrome session that locks the screen mid-recording would show the exact browser behaviour.

evidence: pipeline:src/blueprint_pipeline/atlas_privacy_screen.py:49-50 hand-copied version list; HEAD adds 2026-11-21.1 and 2026-11-22.1 (7d8b532), release cbff06b lacks them (IP-07)

webapp CI run 44852074284: Terms and Privacy 2026-11-21.1 went live 2026-11-21T01:45Z
pipeline:src/blueprint_pipeline/artisan_provider_choice.py:39 a second hand-copied list (to 2026-11-18.1)
findings.today: Builds on IP-07. Since the website moved to Privacy 2026-11-21.1, the running Pipeline release does not know that version, so it blurs faces in frames sent to World Labs. The first decision for a capture is sealed and kept, so those jobs stay blurred after the fix deploys. Privacy is safe. The cost is a different, possibly worse room for those jobs than doctrine promises, and every future Privacy wording change silently flips new jobs to blurred until someone edits two Python lists and deploys.
findings.should: The website states in the signed grant whether this job's frames are blurred, and the Pipeline obeys it.
findings.proposal: WebApp adds face_blur: false|true to the signed Atlas authority from its own version table; the Pipeline reads that field and falls back to blurring when it is missing. findings.title: Every deploy, even one that changes only tests or documents, rebuilds every in-flight job
evidence: pipeline:scripts/operator_door.py:98 NON_RUNTIME_PATHS = ('docs/launch-readiness/',)
pipeline:docs/runbooks/beta-operations.md:671-676 each deploy retires each in-flight website attempt: about 15 min of preparation then about an hour of activation
door-status.json deploys.recent_receipts: d0a41f0 2026-11-19T20:16Z, 1e6283d 20:59Z, 5c91221 23:16Z, 03dcd29 2026-11-20T03:09Z, cbff06b 17:49Z (5 deploys in 21.5 h)
cmd: git diff --name-only cbff06b HEAD -> 22 files, 13 under tests/ and 5 docs; only 4 runtime files
pipeline:docs/runbooks/beta-operations.md:1170-1180 adoption across a deploy is off by default and only SSH from the owner's Mac can turn it on
findings.today: A deploy retires and rebuilds every website attempt that has not yet launched paid work, whether or not the deploy touched its code. Only docs/launch-readiness/ is exempt. On 2026-11-19/20 five deploys landed in 21.5 hours, two of them 43 minutes apart. A job in flight then restarts about 75 minutes of work each time. Paid work is safe: the door parks a deploy while paid stages run (up to 285 min) and each paid call keeps its receipt.
findings.should: A deploy that changes no code the job runs leaves the job alone.
findings.proposal: Widen NON_RUNTIME_PATHS to tests/, docs/, *.md and .github/ (the existing test that guards the list will check it). Then turn on BLUEPRINT_RELEASE_PREPARATION_ADOPTION once, as the runbook describes.
findings.user_result: The site's simulation arrives up to an hour sooner on days with several deploys.
findings.risk: A test-only deploy skips rebuilding, which is the point; adoption is a host setting the owner must make.
findings.requirement_source: D-08 deploy policy and release binding (docs/architecture/release-binding.md); rebuilding for non-runtime files has source nobody

findings.title: Several stuck states have only an operator command or a deploy as the way forward
evidence: pipeline:docs/runbooks/beta-operations.md:64-73 failed or parked Atlas jobs: 'Nothing steps a parked job again'; door selected-handoff --atlas-retry
pipeline:docs/runbooks/beta-operations.md:117 scene_intake_authority_expired: 'Owner decision. Plan, then apply, door extend-scene-execution-window'
door-status.json capacity.stall.checks.scene_progression.dispositions: execution_window 9, rights 30, terminal 13
pipeline:docs/runbooks/beta-operations.md:114-115 spend_unproven: 'Settle by hand'; dispatcher_lost: read the journal
pipeline:docs/runbooks/beta-operations.md:57 website_preparation_blueprint_fault: 'Fix the cause in a release ... the fix must be live before' the window's last two hours
pipeline:docs/runbooks/beta-operations.md:138-140 a preparation that fails six times 'is then left as it is'
pipeline:docs/runbooks/beta-operations.md:154-155 'The stall alarm does not read this file yet' (recovery failures)
findings.today: Doctrine says never make a deploy or an operator command the only way to retry. Today these states have no other exit: a parked or failed room build (door --atlas-retry); an expired scene window (door extend-scene-execution-window, 9 intents now); a launch whose spend cannot be proven (settled by hand); a dead dispatcher (read the journal); a fault in Blueprint's code (a deploy before the window's last two hours); a preparation past six retries (waits for the window to end). None of the parked states pages, and the preparation recovery counter is not read by the alarm.
findings.should: Each wait has a timed automatic retry up to the job's deadline, then one message to the site; operator commands only speed things up.
findings.proposal: One PR per stage, smallest first: (a) Atlas: retry a parked job automatically once after each deploy (a release switch already does this since #3664); (b) preparation: after the six retries, keep retrying on the outage schedule until the grant ends; (c) let the stall alarm read .website_preparation_recovery_failures.json. Delete the execution-window extension as a requirement: when it expires the job ends with what it has, as the spending cap already does.
findings.user_result: Jobs no longer wait on a person; the site hears an ending instead of silence.
findings.risk: Automatic retries after a deploy may repeat a refusal; each step keeps its paid receipts, so nothing is bought twice.
findings.requirement_source: doctrine (AGENTS.md: never make a deploy or an operator command the only way to retry) argues against each; the extension requirement cites an owner approval reference

findings.title: One worker heartbeat covers seven loops; a stuck send or outcome loop goes unnoticed
findings.journey_step: B.1 Job sent to companies; A.9 follow-up
evidence: webapp:server/worker.ts:47-59 seven loops, one heartbeat (workerHeartbeat.ts:20, stale after 5 min)
webapp:server/utils/jobAutoSend.ts:131-140 and jobOutcomes.ts:174-183 a 'running' guard with no timeout: one hung await stops that loop forever
webapp:server/utils/jobAutoSend.ts:121 writes automationState/companyAutoSendCursor.updatedAtIso; grep in betaOpsMonitor.ts -> nothing reads it
webapp:server/utils/jobOutcomes.ts:134-167 the outcome sweep records nothing about its runs
findings.today: The worker writes one heartbeat for the whole process. If the automatic send, the outcome questions, the withdrawal or the deletion loop hangs or keeps throwing, the heartbeat stays fresh and nothing alerts. The send loop records when it last ran but nobody reads it.
findings.should: Each loop writes 'last finished at' and the ops monitor alerts when one is overdue.
findings.proposal: Have each start*Worker write opsHeartbeats/<loop> after each finished pass (one helper), and extend checkWorkerHeartbeat to read all seven with their own intervals. Add a per-pass timeout (Promise.race) so a hung pass releases 'running'.
findings.user_result: If sends to companies stop, the owner hears within minutes, not when a site complains.
findings.risk: Six more small Firestore writes per minute.
findings.requirement_source: doctrine 'No person at Blueprint stands between a site's video and an introduction' (the loops must run unattended)

findings.title: The worker config and its log say 'launch forwarder only' while it runs every job loop
evidence: webapp:render.yaml:31-33 'explicitly constrained to Task Evaluation launch reconciliation; unrelated ops processors stay off'
webapp:render.yaml:53-54 BLUEPRINT_TASK_EVALUATION_LAUNCH_FORWARD_ONLY_WORKER=true

findings.user_result: Nobody switches off withdrawals by mistake.
findings.risk: None for behaviour: the flag already does nothing.
findings.requirement_source: nobody (the flag predates the job loops)

This test will fail today on Reply-To, which is the point.
findings.user_result: The next Reply-To-style bug is caught before a site sees it.
findings.risk: Adds a few seconds to the journey.

findings.title: The Pipeline's nightly full lane is red four nights running and guards nothing
evidence: GitHub Actions full-test-lane.yml: runs 44356749345 (11-18), 44576571521 (11-19), 44778664583 (11-20), 44923019149 (11-21, at HEAD 7d8b532) all conclusion failure; 11-14 to 11-17 success

pipeline:.github/workflows/full-test-lane.yml: no failure notification step (grep notify|slack|issue -> none)
inventory IP-12: a different single test fails each night
findings.today: Builds on IP-12. Every beta deploy is an iteration deploy, which does not need the full lane, so four red nights blocked nothing and told nobody. A different single test fails each night, which looks like order or environment flakiness (one failure needs a 'blueprint' Unix group the runner lacks).
findings.should: A test lane either gates something and is kept green, or it does not run.

findings.title: Company clip and simulation passes retry every minute forever, and a job without a package is only a count
evidence: pipeline:src/blueprint_pipeline/website_atlas_preview.py:1121-1133 company_simulation_tick runs inside every Atlas pass; failures counted, never raised
pipeline:src/blueprint_pipeline/website_company_simulation.py:1919-1921 no_source and not_permitted 'are the job's state, not a fault, and stay counts only'
door journal (inventory row 11): company_simulation_no_source 4, not_permitted 2, zero current packages
findings.today: The package step has no deadline and no message. A job whose simulation source never arrives is re-checked every minute for ever and appears only as a number in a journal line. The site and the companies keep seeing a job without a simulation, with nothing saying it will not come.
findings.should: When the job window ends without a simulation, the job page says once that no simulation will be made, and the pass stops looking.
findings.proposal: Stop considering a capture after its job window end (already on the grant), and have the WebApp's window sweep show 'No simulation was made for this job' when no package was recorded. First ask whether the company simulation is needed at all before a company asks for it (IP-01).
findings.user_result: A site knows whether a simulation is coming.
findings.risk: Low; the passes cost CPU only.
findings.requirement_source: owner direction: packet includes a simulation of the site with the success rule

findings.title: Every upload passes through a function kept in a third repository that neither repo tests or deploys
evidence: webapp:README.md:11 and PLATFORM_CONTEXT.md:178-182 BlueprintCapture is kept only for extractFrames, which 'receives every website upload'
webapp:server/utils/websiteLargeVideoBlock.ts:5-8 the WebApp depends on extractFrames' inline size limit (A-05)
webapp:server/utils/websitePreparationWatch.ts:62-63 the only watch: no Pipeline status within 2 h of upload alerts ops
webapp:docs/backend-scaling-architecture-2026-07-20.md:63 'extractFrames has no maxInstances'
findings.today: The step between a site's upload and the Pipeline lives in a repository kept for nothing else, not checked out here, with its own limits the WebApp has to mirror. Its failures are seen only indirectly, two hours later, when the WebApp notices no Pipeline status. That watch works and should stay.
findings.should: The WebApp, which already knows the instant an upload completes, hands the job to the Pipeline itself.
findings.proposal: Have the WebApp's upload-complete handler write the delivery record and publish the Pub/Sub message the listener already reads, then retire extractFrames and the BlueprintCapture repository. Plan it as one PR in each repo after reading extractFrames' outputs.
findings.user_result: One fewer place for an upload to get lost, and one fewer repository to keep.
findings.risk: extractFrames may write records the listener needs (frames index); those must be produced by the Pipeline instead. Unverified until its code is read.
findings.verify_how: Read BlueprintCapture's extractFrames source and the Pipeline listener's required inputs.
findings.requirement_source: nobody (kept from the retired capture app)

good_things.what: The WebApp ends every job itself when its window passes, with no email and a page that says so
good_things.why: No job waits for ever on the Pipeline: the site always gets an ending.

good_things.what: The email outbox: fixed idempotency keys, provider idempotency, 'unknown outcome' rows never re-sent
good_things.why: A worker or web restart never sends an email twice.

good_things.what: Automatic send and outcome questions are idempotent and catch up after downtime
good_things.why: A marker on the job (company_auto_send) and fixed outbox ids per job, company, side and day mean a day of worker downtime delays sends but neither skips nor duplicates them.

good_things.what: The leader lease falls back to Firestore when there is no Redis
good_things.why: Two processes never run the same loop at once even without Redis.

good_things.what: The upload watch: no Pipeline status within 2 h pages ops, and the site page says only that it is taking longer
good_things.why: It catches extractFrames, Pub/Sub and host outages from outside the Pipeline.

good_things.what: The door parks a deploy while paid work is in flight, and each paid call keeps its receipt
good_things.why: A deploy never wastes money already spent.

owner_questions.question: When a scene's execution window expires, should the job end with what it has instead of waiting for your extension?

owner_questions.question: Should a site that closed its job still get the 14, 45 and 90-day questions after an introduction?
